title: Methods for Discerning the Impact of Mucus on Host Defenses Against Viral Infection
author: Corkran, Boboltz, et al.
materials: Fully differentiated human airway epithelial (HAE) cultures at the air‐liquid interface in 12‐well, 12‐mm Transwells (cell growth area = 1.12 cm2; Corning, cat. no. 3460)
Sterile 1× Dulbecco's phosphate‐buffered saline (DPBS), no calcium, no magnesium (Gibco, cat. no. 14190144)
2.0‐µm red carboxylate–modified microspheres (FluoSpheres, Invitrogen, cat. no. F8826)
Biological safety cabinet (BSC) certified for BSL2 work
Single‐channel pipettes and sterile barrier tips for volumes of 1‐1000 µl
Sterile 15‐ml conical tubes or other sterile containerAmicon Ultra 0.5‐ml, 100‐kDa cutoff centrifugal filters (Millipore‐Sigma, cat. no. UFC5100)

Concentrated mucus samples (see Basic Protocol 2)Complete ALI medium: PneumaCult‐ALI basal medium with PneumaCult‐ALI supplement and PneumaCult‐ALI maintenance supplements (StemCell Technologies, cat. no. 05001) plus 1% penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco, cat. no. 15140‐122)Virus of interest with known titerAqueous 8% (w/v) paraformaldehyde, EM grade (EMS, cat. no. 157‐8)
Sterile 50‐ml conical tubesSterile 1.5‐ml tubesPositive‐displacement pipette for volumes up to 100 µlSterile disposable capillary piston tips for positive‐displacement pipette

steps.title: Generate differentiated HAE cultures
steps.instruction: Seed basal airway epithelial cells onto porous Transwell membranes, grow to confluence, then maintain at an air‑liquid interface for approximately 4 weeks to obtain a pseudostratified epithelium that models mucociliary transport.

steps.title: Prepare ALI medium and reagents
steps.instruction: Assemble complete ALI medium by mixing PneumaCult‑ALI basal medium with PneumaCult‑ALI supplement and PneumaCult‑ALI maintenance supplements (StemCell Technologies, cat. no. 05001) and add 1 % penicillin/streptomycin (Gibco, cat. no. 15140‑122). Gather concentrated mucus samples (per Basic Protocol 2), the virus of interest with a known titer, and aqueous 8 % (w/v) paraformaldehyde, EM grade (EMS, cat. no. 157‑8). Keep sterile 15‑ml conical tubes, sterile 50‑ml conical tubes, sterile 1.5‑ml tubes, Amicon Ultra 0.5‑ml 100‑kDa centrifugal filters (Millipore‑Sigma, cat. no. UFC5100), a positive‑displacement pipette for volumes up to 100 µl, and disposable capillary piston tips ready.

steps.title: Collect apical washes and fix cultures
steps.instruction: After infection, perform apical washes to determine infectious viral titer or viral genome copy number at desired time points. Then fix cultures en face using the 8 % paraformaldehyde solution and proceed with staining according to the referenced protocol.

steps.title: Record mucus transport videos
steps.instruction: Add fluorescent microspheres to the apical surface of the ALI cultures. Using video microscopy, capture movies of particle motion across the surface. Later analyze the videos with particle image velocimetry to calculate mucus transport velocity.

steps.title: Record ciliary beat frequency videos
steps.instruction: Using bright‑field microscopy, acquire videos of the apical surface of the HAE cultures. These recordings will be processed later to quantify ciliary beat frequency.

steps.title: Analyze MCT data (optional method)
steps.instruction: Process the mucus‑transport videos with the TrackerDriver_20180312_MCC.m code. To change particle discrimination, set the variable particleDiscriminationMethod to 1, 2, or 3: method 2 uses a brightness threshold and input particle size; method 1 uses particle radius of gyration, brightness, and eccentricity; method 3 applies method 1 parameters in batch across multiple videos.
